sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Document Automation and E-Signature Authentication

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; central civil registry and corporate register seated in Panama City)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition, with offshore and fiduciary statutes strongly influenced by U.S. corporate practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
Panama–Mexico Free Trade Agreement with investment chapter
Panama–South Korea Income Tax Treaty (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations) and Executive Decree No. 21 of 28 May 1996; Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended by Law No. 62 of 2017 and Law No. 70 of 2019, implemented by Executive Decree No. 406 of 30 October 2020; Law No. 20 of 24 April 2013 and Executive Decree No. 128 of 14 June 2018 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales), read in light of the Pleno of the Supreme Court of Justice ruling of 27 January 2022 invalidating the public-posting elements of the UBO registry while preserving the Financial Intelligence Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) investigatory access; mandatory CDD rules of the UAF binding on registered agents and foundation service providers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter and Regulations (Carta Fundacional y Reglamento), including appointment of the Foundation Council and statement of initial endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública del Primer Circuito de Panamá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial protocol certification by the Panamanian Notary (internal authentication, no apostille required within Panama)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate founder or corporate beneficiary, and authorizing corporate resolutions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the founder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama acceded by Law 38 of 11 June 2007, in force since 30 October 2008) or, for non-Hague states, Panamanian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder) appointing the Panamanian resident agent and the Foundation Council members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Panamanian Consular Legalization, followed by filing with the Registro Público

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of identity documents (passport or national ID) of the Founder, Beneficiaries, Protector and Council members for the AML/CDD file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport-issuing or civil registry authority of the respective country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification in country of origin plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; bank-grade verification acceptable for UAF files

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance screening of every Founder, Council member, Protector, Beneficiary and any documented economic beneficiary against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and FIU/UAF published notices; PEP status assessed under Law 23 of 2015 and UAF circular criteria, with enhanced due diligence required for persons holding, or having held within the previous 12 months, significant public office in any jurisdiction; screening results documented in the AML file, retained for at least 5 years after termination of the relationship, and refreshed upon any change in beneficial ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (SRP) — electronic name reservation and availability certificate (Constancia de Nombre) through the official SRP e-services portal at https://www.registro.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the mandatory language of the register; foundation names must be expressed in Latin-script characters; any proposed name must be distinctive (not identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered entity) and may be presented in English or a Western-European transliteration provided a Spanish translation is recorded in the founding documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fideicomiso / Trust / Fondo de Inversión / Mutual Fund
Cruz Roja / Red Cross / Lotería Nacional / Policía
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written Recurso de Reposición (reconsideration) with the Director General of the Registro Público within five (5) working days of notification, invoking Law 38 of 2001 (Articles 150–159); if the Registry maintains its decision, a Recurso de Apelación may be lodged with the SRP Board of Directors (Junta Directiva) within the following five (5) working days; alternatively, the applicant may submit a revised name reservation with a new Constancia fee. A favorable appeal reinstates the original priority date; the 30-day reservation window is not extended unless an appeal is pending in good faith.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permissible for mail-forwarding, administrative coordination and the registered-office address, provided the PIF retains a licensed Panamanian resident agent (law firm or fiduciary) with a physical office in Panama; banks and the UAF will nevertheless require the economic location and management coordinates of the real team for CDD purposes, and a purely virtual structure will not alone satisfy economic-substance expectations if the PIF receives Panamanian-source income.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantitative risk for this LegalTech SaaS profile: approximately 8–12% probability per operational year of an unannounced UAF or Registro Público spot-check; risk increases materially upon a qualifying high-risk transaction, an AML trigger event, or any mismatch between declared UBO records and filed foundation documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and reservation (Constancia de Nombre)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff schedule of the Registro Público (fixed fee per name search)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting and protocoling of Foundation Charter and Regulations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaría Pública del Primer Circuito de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff scale under Law 53 of 2015; prevailing market range USD 200–500 for non-quantifiable endowment

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration and inscription of the Private Interest Foundation (inscripción) at the Registro Público
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration tariff based on declared endowment (sliding scale; approximate for a nominal USD 10,000 endowment)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed resident agent service, year 1, including statutory registered-office address
Legal drafting of Foundation Regulations, Council appointments, Protector powers and e-signature service agreements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a LegalTech SaaS foundation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML due-diligence file, PEP/OFAC/UN/EU screening and Law 23 onboarding certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per structure (no public statutory tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of English-language source documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-page tariff of the certification authority; market estimate USD 300 for a standard incorporation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign founder/corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the document's country of origin / Panamanian consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document governmental tariff; market estimate USD 40–60 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual office and commercial-substance file set-up (mail forwarding plus inspection-ready records)
Initial annual government fee of Private Interest Foundations under Law 25 of 1995
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos / National Treasury
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed fee (B/.250.00), due from the second year; first-year payment prorated at registration or on the first anniversary

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial foundation endowment contribution (capital injection, not a fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Depositary bank holding the PIF account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Capital contribution per Foundation Charter; no statutory minimum under Law 25 of 1995, USD 10,000 is prevailing market practice for a substantive LegalTech SaaS structure

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), Articles 10-21 and 36, as implemented by Executive Decree 48 of 13 December 1995; supplementary notarial rules of the Panama Civil Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Legal Persons Department, Private Interest Foundations Section.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Constitution of a Private Interest Foundation (Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado) together with the Foundation Regulations (Reglamento).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25 of 1995 sets no statutory minimum paid-up capital, but Article 21 requires the initial endowment to be sufficient for the Foundation's objects. Registry and market practice for a low-risk legal-tech foundation: US$10,000.00 initial endowment. No statutory escrow account applies; the endowment need only be recorded in the charter and demonstrably available to the Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, matter 1: the Founder's subscribed endowment of US$10,000.00 is accepted, recorded as the Foundation's patrimony, and certified sufficient for the objects of cloud document automation and e-signature authentication (ISIC 6201). RESOLVED, matter 2: the registered office is fixed at the resident agent's address in Panama City, ratified as agent under Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED, matter 3: [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed to the Foundation Council as President, Secretary, and Treasurer, with full authority to administer assets, open bank accounts, engage payment processors (including Stripe and credit card acquirers), execute commercial SaaS contracts, and instruct counsel. RESOLVED, matter 4: all formation acts performed by the resident agent and founding officers are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Circuit of Panama (Notaría de Circuito de Panamá), acting with the mandatory participation of a licensed Panama Resident Agent attorney.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Deed and the Reglamento in compliance with Law 25 of 1995, Articles 10-18. Confirm name availability, identify the Founder and initial endowment, and execute the deed before a Panamanian notary. The Founder may act personally or by duly notarized and apostilled power of attorney. The notary protocols the deed for presentation to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Foundation name availability certificate from the Public Registry
Notarized and apostilled passport copy of the Founder
Original power of attorney where the Founder does not appear personally
Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) approved by the Founder
Evidence of identity and license of the Resident Agent (Panamanian attorney)
Statement of initial endowment of US$10,000.00
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable, lodge a new name reservation and re-execute the deed. If the notary raises a substantive defect, execute a corrective document (Escritura Aclaratoria) before the same notary before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Legal Persons Department, Private Interest Foundations Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the protocolized testimonio of the Foundation Deed together with the presentation power (Poder de Presentación) and pay the official arancel scaled to the endowment amount. The Registry conducts legal review (visto); upon approval, it issues the certified inscribed copy (Copia Inscrita), which constitutes the Foundation's certificate of existence.
required_dossiers: Protocolized testimonio of the Foundation Deed and Regulations
Poder de Presentación executed by the Founder
Receipt of payment of the registry inscription arancel
Notarial certification of the Foundation Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a 'visto' query, file a written response curing the objection within the Registry's granted term; if the defect is substantive, execute an amendment deed (Escritura de Modificación) and re-present it for inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directorate General of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Unified Taxpayer Registry (RUC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foundation in the RUC and obtain the tax identification number (NIT) and tax domicile. Select the electronic invoicing service for legal-tech services. Due to Panama's territorial tax system, only Panamanian-source SaaS revenue is taxable; the registration is nonetheless mandatory for banking and local contracting.
required_dossiers: Certified Copia Inscrita from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Foundation Deed and Regulations
RUC application form signed by the Resident Agent
Registered power of attorney for DGI representation
Receipt of payment of any applicable one-time inscription fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI issues a 'prevención' for missing documentation, cure by sworn statement and re-submission through the DGI online portal, attaching the authenticated power of attorney and corrected RUC form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá), Municipal Revenues Directorate (Dirección de Rentas Municipales).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación for the registered office address. Service-only legal-tech SaaS activity is subject to the standard municipal operating notice, not to an industrial license regime. The Resident Agent's office-service or lease agreement constitutes evidence of the fiscal address. The aviso must be renewed annually.
required_dossiers: RUC registration certificate
Copia Inscrita of the Foundation
Lease or registered-office service agreement from the Resident Agent
Municipal Aviso de Operación form filed through the municipal online portal
No sectoral statutory license required for ISIC 6201 services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality queries the address or zoning classification, submit the Resident Agent's service contract or actual leasehold, pay any assessed municipal surcharge, and re-file the aviso in the corrected circuit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization of Foundation Books and Good Standing Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Books Legalization Section; certified by the Resident Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the bound minutes book of the Foundation Council and the accounting/inventory book. Present both books to the Registry for legalization (foja-by-foja stamping). Obtain the Certificado de Persona Jurídica (good standing certificate), which evidences valid existence and representative powers for banking and commercial counterparties.
required_dossiers: Official application form for book legalization
Bound minutes book and accounting book with prefatory inscription
Copia Inscrita and RUC certificate
Receipt of payment of the legalization arancel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the books for formatting or pagination defects, obtain replacement bound books, pay a further arancel, and re-present for legalization; the good standing certificate can be re-issued upon cure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no manufacturing or industrial operation is contemplated. Supervisory coordination: Ministry of Government (Ministerio de Gobierno) for foundation oversight; optional voluntary e-signature accreditation regime under Law 51 of 2003 does not condition the activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Operating Notice (Aviso de Operación) issued by the Municipality of Panama; no sectoral statutory license applies to ISIC 6201 cloud document automation and e-signature authentication, and no industrial manufacturing permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente, MiAMBIENTE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based software and e-signature services are not listed in the mandatory EIA categories of Executive Decree 123 of 20 August 2020 or Law 41 of 1998; a letter of environmental exemption (Carta de Exención) is obtainable if a landlord, bank, or counterparty requires environmental standing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater, VOC, or particulate emissions. Compliance with municipal domestic sewage and potable water ordinances and with Law 6 of 5 February 2018 on integrated solid waste management; all end-of-life IT equipment (servers and e-signature tokens) must be delivered to MiAMBIENTE-authorized e-waste recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Panama Fire Department (Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá) Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for the leased office; Ministry of Health (MINSA) occupational-health and hygiene clearance for office workplaces under the Sanitary Code (Law 14 of 1986) and applicable workplace regulations; structural and electrical load confirmation of the premises prior to installation of servers or co-located terminal equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of Panama; official tax portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa; electronic taxpayer services portal: https://sede.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must first be duly constituted and registered in the Registro Público de Panamá through a foundation deed (escritura constitutiva) or private instrument authenticated by a licensed attorney and a Panama Resident Agent. After registration, the Resident Agent files the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) application with the DGI through the Sede Electrónica, attaching the registered foundation deed, certified copy of the foundation charter, resolution appointing the foundation council, identification of foundation council members and the Resident Agent, and proof of registered address. No physical presence or power-of-attorney travel by foreign founders or foreign beneficiaries is required. The DGI issues a single RUC that is used simultaneously for income tax, ITBMS, and other fiscal identifiers. If the PIF engages in Panama-source taxable activities, it must also obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación before issuing invoices or receiving taxable income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no 'check-the-box' election. A PIF is treated as a separate juridical person with territorial tax liability: only Panama-source income is subject to Panamanian income tax; foreign-source income remains outside Panamanian taxation if it is not derived from activities carried out in Panama. The PIF may elect the simplified small taxpayer ITBMS regime (pequeño contribuyente) if annual Panamanian-source gross turnover does not exceed B/.36,000, using a fixed deemed-credit rate instead of the standard accrual ITBMS. For offshore LegalTech/SaaS services, the PIF may document its ITBMS records as zero-rated export services when all statutory requirements are met. No hybrid mismatch check-the-box elections or similar statutory classifications are available under Panamanian law; foreign entity classifications are governed by the foundation instrument and the residence of the founder for tax avoidance purposes, subject to general anti-abuse rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a las Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panamanian value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 annual Panamanian-source gross turnover (Balboa at par with USD) is the statutory threshold for the simplified small taxpayer ITBMS regime; regular ITBMS registration is mandatory above this threshold. In practice, any entity that imports goods or performs taxable commercial transactions in Panama must obtain an RUC regardless of turnover. Non-resident suppliers of digital services are also subject to ITBMS on supplies effectively used or enjoyed in Panama and must comply with DGI registration or withholding obligations without the benefit of the small-taxpayer local threshold where Panamanian law requires tax collection by payment facilitators or electronic platforms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under Panama's DGI 'Facturación Electrónica' (SFE) system is in force. All ITBMS-registered taxpayers must issue e-invoices by transmitting the invoice data to the DGI SFE platform in real time at or before issuance and receive a unique authorization code and a digital QR/digital stamp from the DGI. The exchange uses DGI-approved software, an API, or the DGI free web portal with a structured XML/JSON payload defined by DGI technical guidance. The DGI does not recognize as valid any invoice lacking the online authorization; late transmission, unauthorized invoices, or erroneous zero-rating codes are rejected and subject to penalties and surcharges. The timeline of mandatory implementation is phased by taxpayer category, with large, middle, and small taxpayers progressively integrated through DGI resolutions issued since 2022.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under ITBMS applies to: (1) tangible goods physically exported from Panama through a definitive customs export process; and (2) services supplied to non-resident customers for use, exploitation, or benefit wholly outside Panama, including cloud document automation, e-signature authentication, and LegalTech SaaS services, provided the service is not performed in Panama and no Panamanian taxable nexus is created. The PIF must prove that the customer is non-resident, the digital platform or service is delivered outside Panama, and all revenue originates from abroad. The zero-rating must be reflected in the ITBMS monthly declaration and supported by permanent documentation retained for at least the statutory limitation period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Definitive Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación Definitiva) filed with the Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) through the Panama Single Window
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical movement of goods from Panama; for SaaS/digital services, a signed digital service certificate and user-delivery report in lieu of transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of payment in foreign currency from the non-resident customer in a Panamanian bank account
Commercial invoice or export invoice expressly stating 'Gravado 0% ITBMS - Exportación'
Signed foundation customer contract / LegalTech SaaS agreement with payment, access, and IP-location evidence demonstrating use outside Panama
Copy of the PIF's RUC registration and the ITBMS declaration pages showing the zero-rated export line items
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may reclassify zero-rated export transactions as taxable Panama-source supplies if the documentation, user-location evidence, or 180-day receipt/repatriation proof is inadequate. In such cases the DGI will assess the undeclared 7% ITBMS, default interest at the legal tax rate, monthly surcharges up to the statutory maximum (frequently up to 50% of the tax), and statutory fines for inaccurate filings. Fraudulent export zero-rating, forged customs declarations, false bills of lading, or sham service contracts constitute tax and customs offences under the Código Fiscal and Panamanian customs legislation, exposing the PIF, its officers, and its Resident Agent to criminal sanctions, retrospective clawback for the full period not yet prescribed, cancellation of e-invoice authorization privileges, and removal from exporter registries.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Banking and financial licensing supervisor; the Panama Balboa serves as the onshore exchange-rate anchor to the US Dollar under full dollarization. The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) exercises no foreign exchange allocation authority and the Panamanian Tax Administration (DGI) does not administer exchange control approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with no central-bank foreign exchange control decree, no surrender requirement for export proceeds, and no convertibility bottleneck for current or capital account flows. Capital account convertibility is effectively free for foundational contributions, PIF asset transfers, and foreign-held beneficiary disbursements, subject to bank-level AML/Source-of-Wealth due diligence. Profit and dividend remittances from Panamanian business activities are routed under the territorial tax model; the 10% dividend tax (Law 52 of 2017) applies to distributions sourced from Panama- sourced taxable profits, while amounts attributable to foreign-source income and passive non-Panama activities can be distributed without additional tax withholding. A PIF is not a commercial operating company and its foundation council distributions are generally private patrimony transfers rather than dividends, so remittance barriers are limited to bank proof-of-foundation-validity and internal compliance classification rather than government FX authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation to surrender, repatriate, or convert export receipts. The Panama legal framework contains no mandatory conversion ratio, no 90/180-day export settlement calendar, and no central bank ledger requirement for foreign currency invoices. The relevant compliance burden is bank-side: invoices and customs documentation supporting services under ISIC 6201 must be preserved in the client dossier for AML transaction-scope testing, but the PIF can retain all USD and non-USD funds in local or offshore accounts without forced conversion. The same regime applies to cloud automation and e-signature licensing revenue, which is treated as foreign-source service income if the customer, execution, and contractual nexus sit outside Panama's territory.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) accounts have marginal viability for a Panama PIF. The SBP maintains a closed licensing perimeter for deposit-taking and e-money services, so a foreign EMI cannot hold the PIF treasury without either a Panama branch license or a local license as a 'Sociedad de Emisión y Pago Electrónico'. A low-risk LegalTech SaaS PIF may use a licensed Panamanian EMI as a payment-acceptance gateway, but settlement of STIRPE credit-card receivables must be collected through a Panamanian bank account that enjoys USD clearing capability. Viability rating: LOW as a primary treasury conduit and MEDIUM only as an auxiliary pay-in gateway subject to SBP-regulated third-party clearing and full PCI-DSS controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PIF founders and foundation council members are generally required to appear physically before a Panamanian notary public to execute the foundation charter and private foundation bylaws. For bank onboarding, many Tier-1 banks mandate an in-person interview with at least two beneficial owners or council members at their corporate banking floor in Panama City; remote onboarding is selectively available only for existing relationships and low-risk non-operating structures. The LegalTech SaaS PIF should plan for a two-to-three day physical presence milestone at the bank and notary to achieve unconditional account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share or undefined beneficial owner exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized foundation charter, declaration of council members, complete chain of beneficial-ownership attestation, audited or certified identification of all foundation council participants, and a clear statement that the PIF has no bearer participation rights or anonymous certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ENEV protocol flag due to private-interest-foundation opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Panamanian law firm confirming PIF validity, foundation registration certificate, common seal, simple foundation bylaws, and an operational narrative for ISIC 6201 SaaS activities showing real economic substance and no nominee concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus of foreign beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificates, passport copies, proof of legitimate source of wealth and funds, independent credit/corporate search highlighting no PEP status, and a beneficiary-bank reference letter from the originating financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payment flows through Stripe and credit-card acquirers without clear treasury narration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreement with Stripe, sub-processor disclosure, projected settlement statements, payment policy documentation, cancellation/refund protocol, and a treasury flow map demonstrating that credit-card receivables settle directly into the designated Panamanian operational account without intermediary shell routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection from non-resident founders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds evidence including bank statements, income tax receipts, formation-of-capital declaration under the foundation charter, a signed contribution letter, and confirmation that the capital funds are not derived from proceeds of crime, sanctions evasion, or unexplained third-party transfers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions to the PA_PIF must be wired in USD through SWIFT using MT103 with a precise OBI/remittance field: 'Capital Contribution to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF – Foundation Charter Date – Council Resolution'. Panama does not require exchange-control approval; however, the receiving bank will apply a beneficiary-profile screening and OFAC/UESAN sanctions filter. The PIF treasury should request a pre-account-opening wire test with a nominal USD amount, maintain proof of the founder's bank, and document the transaction as a pure donation/patrimony contribution rather than a sales invoice payment. For directorships and SaaS license sales, the same wire should carry the contract invoice number and 'ISIC 6201 subscription/e-signature service revenue' reference.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for legal-contract automation vendor payments, independent contractor compensation, and licensing costs should be executed via SWIFT MT103 through the Panamanian bank's USD clearing correspondent in the United States. Local USD clearing may use the SBP-operated Panama Banking Clearing Center for same-city checks, but commercial vendor settlements should remain SWIFT-based. For larger transactions requiring title retention or milestone verification, a commercial letter of credit (documentary credit) can be issued through a Panamanian issuing bank with SWIFT MT700/MT720, particularly where the SaaS provider contracts with international data centers or infrastructure suppliers. All outbound payments must be paired with underlying contracts, invoices, and transaction purpose codes prepared in the same document repository as the LegalTech e-signature automation records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated plain-vanilla currency forwards with licensed Panamanian banks for EUR or GBP operational exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offered by international counterparties with a Panama banking relationship, where the PIF's functional currency is USD and settlement occurs in USD
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR) executed under ISDA with a licensed SBP-regulated bank for multi-year SaaS infrastructure commitments
Bank-guaranteed options (call/put USD pairs) for software licensing royalties derived from non-USD markets, if prudently approved by the council
FX swaps with same-day or institutional interbank settlement to cover temporary multi-currency liquidity gaps in SaaS pay-ins via Stripe international cards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax on Private Interest Foundation (Impuesto Anual de Operación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance – Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 5% per month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the tax; two consecutive unpaid years trigger administrative strike-off from the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Update Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each year; within 30 days of any change in beneficial interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance leads to fines ranging from USD 100 to USD 10,000; continued failure may prevent issuance of solvency certificates and result in registry suspension.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for private interest foundations that do not carry out Panama-source business activities. Audit is compulsory only if the foundation's gross annual income exceeds USD 3,000,000 or if it holds a license for financial operations (banking, securities, trust, or collective investments).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian GAAP (Convergence Decree No. 14 of 2011); full IFRS applies to licensed banks, insurers, and securities issuers; other entities may use IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must maintain a current beneficial ownership register. The foundation must notify the agent in writing of any transfer of beneficial rights within 30 days. The agent is required to confirm the foundation's beneficiary details at least annually, before the March 31 franchise tax deadline, and to file any changes in the DGI beneficial ownership report by that same date. This confirmation is separate from (but synchronized with) the annual franchise tax payment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Entitlement Rights
Minute Book containing Resolutions of the Foundation Council and Founder

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 6,000 per review if an audit or certified financial statement is required; not applicable for non-audited PIFs

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama operates a territorial taxation system. Only Panama-source income is subject to corporate income tax at 25%. Tax incentives include: (i) the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) law offering reduced effective rates between 0% and 5% on qualifying foreign-source income for up to 10 years; (ii) Law 57 of 2018 SME incentives with preferential rates of 10% first year and 15% second year for SMEs; (iii) special economic zones like Ciudad del Saber, and Pacific Free Zone; (iv) no withholding tax on foreign-source dividends; (v) foreign-source income is outside scope if not engaged in Panamanian economic activity. No general capital gains discount except real estate prorated rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2002 (Informe de Declaración de Rentas) filed via DGI Portal 'SITIO' (sistema de tramitación en línea) at dgi.gob.pa. Also, Form 2001 for payment of advance tax (anticipo). Registration via Panamanian RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Additionally, quarterly advance payments if annual gross income exceeds USD 1,500,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 2002 due within 3 months after fiscal year end (March 31 for calendar year misalignment). Quarterly advance payments due within one month after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income: total revenue from Panamanian source activities; for SaaS/e-signature income, include revenues from Panamanian clients or services rendered in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Panama-source revenue. Revenue from overseas clients (foreign cloud automation services delivered remotely) is considered foreign-source and excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income (non-taxable): gross amounts from foreign operations qualifying under territorial rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach schedule listing foreign clients, respective contracts, and evidence that services provided from outside Panama. Rely on place of performance / place of use rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: Panama allocable expenses related to Panamanian-source income, e.g. server costs, local affiliate support, direct costs, amortization, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deduct expenses directly attributable to Panama-source income. Deductions for global overhead must follow an documented allocation ratio.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after adjustments and loss carryforwards (max 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply registered tax losses limited to losses generated from Panama-source activities. Foreign losses bereft of tax relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments (anticipos) paid during fiscal year: Form 2001 installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only if PIF registered as taxpayer and paid anticipo; non-resident without PE might be outside obligor scope unless invoicing in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: USD 50 up to 1% per month of tax due; in case of false understatement, penalties from 25% to 200% of omitted tax. Interest accrual at variable rate. Failure to register with DGI or to file nil return can trigger compulsory assessment. Criminal prosecution only for willful evasion under Art. 282-E Criminal Code (term 3–5 years).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by Panamanian companies from Panama-source profits to resident or non-resident shareholders, unless the PIF is a foundation that does not distribute 'dividends' but may distribute (when structured as corporation). If a PIF is organized as a corporation (SA) under Law 32 of 1927, the 10% dividend withholding applies. If pure foundation, distributions to beneficiaries are not subject to dividend WHT if not classified as Panamanian-source corporate profits but may be taxable to foreign beneficiary in resident country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has no comprehensive network of DTA under OECD model; only 4 signed treaties (Barbados, Mexico, Luxembourg, Qatar) not all in force. DTA relief protocol: obtain beneficial owner certificate issued by DGI (Certificado de Residencia/ORI), complete IRS Form for Panama, request reduced WHT before payment, submit TRC within the year; if not, claim refund under domestic legislation. For non-treaty foreign beneficiary, domestic 10% dividend WHT applies with no exception except reinvestment in Panama-listed securities or offshore distribution exclusion.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for technology or software licenses paid to non-residents attract 12.5% WHT if economic use is in Panama; interest on internal or cross-border loans paid by Panamian entity to a non-resident is subject to 12.5% WHT unless said interest relates to foreign-source loans or banks registered in Panama. Treaty rates under Mexico DTA: dividends 5% if 10% ownership, royalties 10%, interest 10%. No treaty with US/EU means statutory rates apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panamanian TP documentation thresholds under Decree No. 356 of 2016 and Resolution No. 58-2018: entities with gross yearly revenue above USD 3,000,000 or related party transactions equal or above USD 1,000,000 are required to prepare Local File. Master File required for groups with consolidated annual revenue of USD 21,000,000 or more. Full OECD compliant documentation required if part of group with global turnover equal or above USD 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not have legislative ESR mirroring UAE, but since Law 254 of 2021, legal entities (including PIF) must report economic substance on their beneficial ownership declaration. DGI may require justification of business purpose activity with sufficient human/asset presence if the company seeks Panama tax residency or treaty benefits. Lack of substance for a PIF generating SaaS revenue can lead to income reclassification as Panama-source if management and control exercised in Panama or if contracts/funds flow through Panama bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Territorial Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely excluding Panama-source revenue as foreign by routing payments through foreign intermediaries or using sham contracts; understating e-signature transaction volume from Panamanian clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 25% to 200% evaded tax; criminal imprisonment of 3 to 5 years under Article 282-E Código Penal; administrative closure of the entity by DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council may be jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts if they knowingly signed false returns or approved fraudulent distributions; travel bans and asset freezes under Panama ATP/GAFILAT enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating PIF with no physical activity, no employees or assets, only registered address, used to hold international SaaS contracts without any real management in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may pierce through and apply full 25% tax on all worldwide revenues; registration cancellation under Law 254 reporting requirements; AML fines up to USD 50,000 – 100,000; criminal sanctions for abuse of legal personality under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or registered agent may incur personal penalties, revocation of professional license, travel bans and potential seizure of personal assets if found facilitating a sham corporate structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: PIF used as conduit for receipt of SaaS payments from unknown third parties where credit card or wire transfers bypass know your client (KYC) checks; failure to file beneficial ownership declaration under Law 254 of 2021.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000; suspension of PIF rights by Registry; criminal money-laundering penalties up to 12 years imprisonment under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Council members can be personally fined and imprisoned for laundering if they knew or should have known origin of funds, with confiscation of benefits received.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain and Retain Transfer Pricing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border intercompany contracts between PIF and related software vendors / global group entities not complying with arm's length; monthly service fees/royalties outbound without TP study when thresholds exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI can adjust taxable basis and impose penalties between 50% and 100% of transfer pricing adjustment; dedicated penalty under Tax Code Art. 761; if intentional, criminal surcharge may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: No criminal veil pierce for mere TP failure, but directors who neglect documentation can be liable for the penalty by law if shown gross negligence; authorities may move against third-party professional advisers jointly.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Profit Repatriation / Dividend Withholding Non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends (in SA form) or foundation distributions to foreign beneficiaries from Panamanian accumulated earnings without paying or declaring 10% dividend WHT; attempting to classify distribution as tax-free capital or loan without documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unpaid 10% WHT tax with interest; penalties up to 200%; criminal withholding evasion if deliberate; DGI refusal to issue clean tax solvency certificate (Certificado de Paz y Salvo).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and PIF council can be personally liable for withheld taxes under joint liability provisions; preventing bank transfers/sale of assets in Panama to enforce lien.
